title: Michael Dillon On Shanghai — China’s Most Dynamic City - The Wire China
gist: Historian Michael Dillon's new book traces Shanghai's arc from fishing village to China's wealthiest metropolis and key financial centre, framing the city as the through-line of modern Chinese history from the 19th-century foreign concessions to the CCP's founding; the article is a paywalled teaser cut off before further detail.

insights.claim: Historian Michael Dillon's book 'Shanghai: The Story of China's Most Dynamic City' argues Shanghai's transformation from a small fishing village into China's wealthiest metropolis and one of its most important financial centres makes it a central lens for understanding modern Chinese history.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Frames Shanghai's continued role as China's premier financial hub as historically path-dependent rather than incidental, relevant for investors tracking China's financial-centre concentration.
insights.quote: he traces the city’s development from a small fishing village into China’s wealthiest metropolis and one of its most important financial centres
insights.locator: Michael Dillon is a historian of China

insights.claim: Dillon's book positions Shanghai's history as spanning the 19th-century foreign concessions through the birth of the Chinese Communist Party, linking the city's colonial-era commercial infrastructure to the origins of CCP rule.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Underscores Shanghai's dual identity as both the product of foreign capital and the birthplace of the party now regulating that capital — a tension still visible in how Beijing manages the city's financial-sector openness.
insights.quote: from the foreign concessions of the nineteenth century, to the birth of the Chinese Communist Party, war
insights.locator: The book explores Shanghai’s central place in Chinese history
